The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-substituted isatin.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries a CO2H at the meta position relative to the biaryl bond. The second ring has the biaryl bond at one carbon, an OH on the adjacent carbon, and the HN–N= group on the next carbon after that. So the second ring is 2-hydroxy-3-hydrazinyl, with the aryl group at position 1.

**Isatin part.** The oxindole has C=O at C2 and the C3=N hydrazone carbon. The ring nitrogen bears a 3-methylthiophen-2-yl group. The thiophene is drawn with C2 attached to N, a methyl on C3, then C4, C5 and S.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N double bond is drawn with a defined geometry. The NH sits on the lower left of the N, and the C=N carbon is C3 of the oxindole. At C3, the substituent toward C2 (C=O) is on the left and the aromatic ring is on the right.

At the double bond, the top atom (C3) is at about (405, 405) and the lower atom (N) is at about (405, 335). The N's other substituent, NH, is at the left (350, 310). On C3, the carbonyl carbon C2 is at the lower left (345, 440) and the aryl carbon C3a is at the lower right (450, 440). The NH is on the left, the same side as C2 (C=O), which gives Z in the usual priority analysis: on C3, C2 (O,O,N) outranks C3a (C,C,C), so C2 is the higher priority, and NH is on that side.

The SMILES below is written with this geometry, N(H)/N=C3 with C2 on the same side.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3sccc3C)c3ccccc23)c1O

I did not verify the written / and \ marks against the Z assignment by a separate check.
